selection_reason: Consistent with the AI4I case study's model choice: a tree ensemble needs no feature scaling, trains in seconds on this dataset size, and supports exact/fast SHAP explanations via TreeExplainer.

dataset.name: NASA C-MAPSS Turbofan Engine Degradation Simulation (FD001)
dataset.reference: A. Saxena, K. Goebel, D. Simon, N. Eklund, "Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Simulation", PHM08, Denver CO, 2008 (NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence Data Repository)

hyperparameter_tuning.cv_strategy: GroupKFold grouped by unit_number — rows from the same engine never appear in both the train and validation side of a fold. This is the grouped/time-aware split AI4I's static, one-row-per-machine structure cannot support.

feature_engineering_impact.note: Same tuned hyperparameters applied to raw sensor readings vs. rolling-window (mean/std) engineered features, so the delta is attributable to the rolling-window features alone.

next_step: Extend to FD002/FD004 (multiple operating conditions) to test whether the rolling-window feature set generalizes beyond a single flight regime.
